session.composer.busyPlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the message box of an agent session while the agent is busy: a message typed now is saved as a draft, not sent.

session.composer.saveTitle.text: Save this as a draft (Ctrl+Enter or ⌘+Enter). It stays here until you send it
session.composer.saveTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Save draft" button of the message box of an agent session while the agent is busy. Ctrl+Enter and ⌘+Enter are keyboard shortcuts (⌘ is the Mac Command key): keep the key names and the symbol as they are. No final full stop.

session.composer.archivedPlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the message box of an agent session when the conversation is archived and cannot take messages.

session.composer.placeholder.text: Describe a change to any app in plain English. No coding needed.
session.composer.placeholder.description: Placeholder of the message box of an agent session: what to type to the coding agent. "change" is a noun.

session.composer.archivedNote.text: This session is archived. Unarchive it to keep going.
session.composer.archivedNote.description: Note above the message box of an archived agent session, beside an Unarchive button.

session.composer.unarchive.description: Button in the note above the message box of an archived agent session: a verb, brings the conversation back so it can continue.

session.composer.saveNote.text: The agent is still working, so this will be <0>saved as a draft, not sent</0>. Send it from your drafts when it finishes.
session.composer.saveNote.description: Note above the message box of an agent session when the person types while the agent is busy. Keep the <0> tags around the emphasised words.

session.composer.label.description: Accessible name of the message box of an agent session: the person writes to the coding agent here. "Message" is a verb.

session.composer.attach.description: Tooltip and accessible name of the paperclip button beside the message box of an agent session: opens the file chooser.

session.composer.stop.description: Tooltip and accessible name of the square button beside the message box of an agent session while the agent works: a verb, stops the agent.

session.composer.saveAsDraft.description: Accessible name of the button that takes Send's place beside the message box while the agent is busy: saves the typed message for later.

session.composer.saveDraft.description: Visible text of the button that takes Send's place beside the message box while the agent is busy: a verb, saves the typed message for later.

session.composer.sendWaitingLabel.description: Accessible name of the disabled Send button beside the message box of an agent session while attached files are still uploading.

session.composer.send.description: Tooltip and accessible name of the arrow button beside the message box of an agent session: a verb, sends the message to the agent.

session.composer.stopUnavailableTitle.description: Tooltip of the disabled Stop button beside the message box while the agent writes its closing reply.

session.composer.sendWaitingTitle.text: Waiting for your files to upload
session.composer.sendWaitingTitle.description: Tooltip of the disabled Send button beside the message box of an agent session while attached files are still uploading.

session.drafts.label.description: Accessible name of the list of saved drafts above the message box of an agent session: messages typed while the agent was busy and kept for later.

session.drafts.heading_one.description: Line at the top of the list of saved drafts above the message box of an agent session (messages typed while the agent was busy and kept for later). The <0> part is a small upper-case heading; {{count}} is how many drafts are saved. The <1> part is a note beside it: the drafts are stored with the account, so they show on every device the person uses. Keep both pairs of tags, and the middle dot that opens the note.

session.drafts.heading_other.description: Line at the top of the list of saved drafts above the message box of an agent session (messages typed while the agent was busy and kept for later). The <0> part is a small upper-case heading; {{count}} is how many drafts are saved. The <1> part is a note beside it: the drafts are stored with the account, so they show on every device the person uses. Keep both pairs of tags, and the middle dot that opens the note.

session.drafts.locked.text: sending unlocks when the agent finishes
session.drafts.locked.description: Note at the right of the "Saved drafts" heading while the agent is busy: drafts cannot be sent yet. Lower case, no full stop.

session.drafts.ready.description: Note at the right of the "Saved drafts" heading once the agent has finished: the drafts can be sent now.

session.drafts.send.description: Accessible name of the send button on one row in the list of saved drafts above the message box of an agent session (messages typed while the agent was busy and kept for later).

session.drafts.sendBusyTitle.text: The agent is still working. You can send this when it finishes
session.drafts.sendBusyTitle.description: Tooltip of the disabled send button on a saved draft while the agent is busy. No final full stop.

session.drafts.sendTitle.description: Tooltip of the send button on one row in the list of saved drafts above the message box of an agent session (messages typed while the agent was busy and kept for later).

session.drafts.edit.description: Accessible name of the pencil button on one row in the list of saved drafts above the message box of an agent session (messages typed while the agent was busy and kept for later).

session.drafts.editTitle.text: Put this draft back in the box to edit
session.drafts.editTitle.description: Tooltip of the pencil button on a saved draft: the text returns to the message box.

session.drafts.delete.description: Tooltip and accessible name of the bin button on one row in the list of saved drafts above the message box of an agent session (messages typed while the agent was busy and kept for later).

session.stop.slow.text: Stopping is taking longer than expected.
session.stop.slow.description: Status line above the message box of an agent session a few seconds after Stop was pressed and the agent has not stopped yet.

session.stop.stopping.description: Status line above the message box of an agent session right after Stop was pressed.

session.stop.retry.description: Button beside the stopping status line in an agent session: sends the stop request again.

session.drawer.heading.description: Heading and accessible name of the panel opened by the "Changes" button of an agent session. "Changes" is a noun: the code changes this conversation made.

session.drawer.active.description: Small upper-case heading in the panel that lists the code changes made in an agent session, over the change the conversation is working on now.

session.drawer.activeLinePr.description: Small line under the active change's title in the panel that lists the code changes made in an agent session. {{app}} is the app's name, {{number}} the pull request's number, {{change}} the change's own number. "change" is a noun.

session.drawer.linePr.description: Small line under an earlier change's title in the panel that lists the code changes made in an agent session. {{app}} is the app's name, {{number}} the pull request's number.

session.drawer.lineChange.description: Small line under a change's title in the panel that lists the code changes made in an agent session, when it has no pull request. {{app}} is the app's name; "Change" is a noun and {{number}} its number.

session.drawer.checks.description: Line on the active change in the panel that lists the code changes made in an agent session: where its automated checks stand. {{state}} is the server's status word in English, such as passing, failing or running.

session.drawer.openPreview.description: Button on the active change in the panel that lists the code changes made in an agent session: a verb, shows the test build of the app with the change in it.

session.drawer.spec.description: Button on the active change in the panel that lists the code changes made in an agent session: opens the change's plan, the written description of what it will do. A noun.

session.drawer.proposalPage.description: Link on the active change in the panel that lists the code changes made in an agent session: goes to the change's own page in the app's workshop. "Proposal" is a noun.

session.drawer.none.text: No active change. Ask the agent to start one.
session.drawer.none.description: Shown in the panel that lists the code changes made in an agent session when the conversation is not working on any change. "change" is a noun.

session.drawer.earlier.description: Small upper-case heading in the panel that lists the code changes made in an agent session, over the changes the conversation worked on before the current one.

session.drawer.switchTo.description: Button on an earlier change in the panel that lists the code changes made in an agent session: makes that change the one the conversation works on.

session.screenLabel.description: Accessible name of the full-screen agent session: the conversation with Homeroom's coding agent.

menu.suggestImprovement.description: The one button at the top of the Homeroom menu (the sheet opened from the Homeroom mark): opens the dialog for sending a suggestion or bug report about the app on screen.

menu.update.platformReady.description: Row in the Homeroom menu (the sheet opened from the Homeroom mark) when a new version of Homeroom itself, not of the app on screen, is ready. A "Reload" button ends the row; pressing the row reloads the page.

menu.update.appReady.description: Row in the Homeroom menu (the sheet opened from the Homeroom mark) when the app on screen has a new released version. A "Reload" button ends the row; pressing the row reloads the app. {{app}} is the app's name.

menu.update.appReadyUnnamed.description: The same row as menu.update.appReady, when the app's name is not known yet: the app on screen has a new released version. A "Reload" button ends the row; pressing the row reloads the app.

menu.update.action.description: Button at the end of the Homeroom menu's update-ready rows ("Homeroom has an update", "<app> has an update"): reloads onto the new version. A verb. It is a button on phones and computers alike, so it says Reload rather than Tap or Click.

menu.update.platformDownloading.text: Homeroom is downloading an update. You can reload once it’s ready.
menu.update.platformDownloading.description: Small note with a spinner in the Homeroom menu (the sheet opened from the Homeroom mark) while a new version of Homeroom itself is being downloaded. A row to reload takes its place once it is ready.

menu.update.platformBuilding.description: Small note with a spinner in the Homeroom menu (the sheet opened from the Homeroom mark) while a new version of Homeroom itself is being deployed.

menu.update.appBuilding.text: An update to {{app}} is on its way.
menu.update.appBuilding.description: Small note with a spinner in the Homeroom menu (the sheet opened from the Homeroom mark) while a new version of the app on screen is being deployed. {{app}} is the app's name.

menu.update.appBuildingUnnamed.text: An update to this app is on its way.
menu.update.appBuildingUnnamed.description: The same note as menu.update.appBuilding, when the app's name is not known yet: a new version of the app on screen is being deployed.

menu.row.state.working.description: State pill on a row of the person's changes in progress, in the Homeroom menu: the coding agent is working on this change right now.

menu.row.state.handedOff.description: State pill on a row of the person's changes in progress, in the Homeroom menu: the work was handed to a coding tool on the person's own machine, so Homeroom cannot see its progress.

menu.row.state.needsYou.description: State pill on a row of the person's changes in progress, in the Homeroom menu: the agent is waiting for the person's answer.

menu.row.state.ready.description: State pill on a row of the person's changes in progress, in the Homeroom menu: the agent is idle and the change is ready for the person to continue.

menu.row.unread.description: Accessible name of the small dot on a row of the person's changes in progress, in the Homeroom menu: something happened on that change that the person has not seen.

menu.row.status.working.description: Status word in the small grey caption under the title of a change in progress, in the Homeroom menu and the app menu: the coding agent is working on it right now.

menu.row.status.needsYou.description: Status word in the small grey caption under the title of a change in progress, in the Homeroom menu and the app menu: the agent is waiting for the person's answer.

menu.row.status.handedOff.description: Status word in the small grey caption under the title of a change in progress, in the Homeroom menu and the app menu: the work was handed to a coding tool on the person's own machine and it is not known which one.

menu.row.caption.description: Small grey caption under the title of a change in progress, in the Homeroom menu's list of changes on other apps: which app the change belongs to, then where it stands. {{app}} is the app's name; {{status}} is a short status already worded ("Working…", "Needs you", "Handed off") or the name of the coding tool that holds the work (Claude Code, Codex). Keep the middle dot between them.

menu.row.sessionFallback.description: Title of a change in progress in the Homeroom menu when it has no title, pull request or branch name. "Session" is a working session with the coding agent; {{number}} is its number.

menu.row.workOrderFallback.description: Title, in the Homeroom menu, of work handed to a coding tool on the person's own machine when it has no title. A work order is that hand-off; {{number}} is its number.

topicBack.messages.description: Text of the back chip at the top of a request's or proposal's page when it was opened from a conversation: it returns to the Messages screen. The name of that screen.

topicBack.workshop.description: Text of the back chip at the top of a request's or proposal's page: it returns to the project's Workshop, the board of its changes and requests. The name of that tab, a noun.

appContext.about.members_one.description: Pill beside the builders' avatars in the About pane of the app menu (the sheet opened from the app's name in the header): how many people are in the app's community. {{formatted}} is that number written with digit grouping, for example 1,284; {{count}} is the same number and only selects the plural form.

appContext.about.members_other.description: Pill beside the builders' avatars in the About pane of the app menu (the sheet opened from the app's name in the header): how many people are in the app's community. {{formatted}} is that number written with digit grouping, for example 1,284; {{count}} is the same number and only selects the plural form.

appContext.about.version.app.description: Plain line at the foot of the About pane naming the running version. {{version}} is a short code such as a1b2c3d. Used for an app.

appContext.about.version.appDeploying.description: Plain line at the foot of the About pane naming the running version. {{version}} is a short code such as a1b2c3d. Used for an app while a newer version is being deployed.

appContext.about.version.appDeployingOnl.description: Plain line at the foot of an app's About pane while its first version is being deployed and there is no version code to show yet.

appContext.about.version.platform.description: Plain line at the foot of the About pane naming the running version. {{version}} is a short code such as a1b2c3d. Used for Homeroom itself.

appContext.about.version.platformDeployi.description: Plain line at the foot of the About pane naming the running version. {{version}} is a short code such as a1b2c3d. Used for Homeroom itself while a newer version is being deployed.
Plain line at the foot of Homeroom's own About pane while a version is being deployed and there is no version code to show.

appContext.about.stat.apps_one.description: Label under a large number on one of the three cards in Homeroom's own About pane. The number is drawn above it; {{count}} only selects the plural form. Lower case. Counts the apps on Homeroom.

appContext.about.stat.apps_other.description: Label under a large number on one of the three cards in Homeroom's own About pane. The number is drawn above it; {{count}} only selects the plural form. Lower case. Counts the apps on Homeroom.

appContext.about.stat.members_one.description: Label under a large number on one of the three cards in Homeroom's own About pane. The number is drawn above it; {{count}} only selects the plural form. Lower case. Counts the people on Homeroom.

appContext.about.stat.members_other.description: Label under a large number on one of the three cards in Homeroom's own About pane. The number is drawn above it; {{count}} only selects the plural form. Lower case. Counts the people on Homeroom.

appContext.about.stat.live_one.description: Label under a large number on one of the three cards in Homeroom's own About pane. The number is drawn above it; {{count}} only selects the plural form. Lower case. Counts the changes that have been released; an adjective.

appContext.about.stat.live_other.description: Label under a large number on one of the three cards in Homeroom's own About pane. The number is drawn above it; {{count}} only selects the plural form. Lower case. Counts the changes that have been released; an adjective.

appContext.about.contributor.unknown.description: Stands in for a contributor's username in the About pane's list when the server sent none. Lower case; it is shown after an @ sign.

appContext.about.open.resume.description: Main button in the About pane of the app menu (the sheet opened from the app's name in the header), beside "Add to My apps": a verb, goes back to this app, which is still open in the background.

appContext.about.open.open.description: Main button in the About pane of the app menu (the sheet opened from the app's name in the header), beside "Add to My apps": a verb, opens the app.

appContext.about.open.spinningUp.description: Main button in the About pane of the app menu (the sheet opened from the app's name in the header), beside "Add to My apps": shown disabled while the app is being created and cannot be opened yet.

appContext.about.open.notRunning.description: Main button in the About pane of the app menu (the sheet opened from the app's name in the header), beside "Add to My apps": shown disabled when the app failed to start.

appContext.about.open.unavailable.description: Main button in the About pane of the app menu (the sheet opened from the app's name in the header), beside "Add to My apps": shown disabled when the app cannot be opened and its state is not known.

appContext.invite.error.generic.description: Error in the Invite pane of the app menu when making, reading or turning off an invite link failed and the server gave no reason.

appContext.invite.detail.joined_one.description: The second line on a row of the list of invite links in the Invite pane of the app menu: how many people actually got in through this link. {{count}} is that number.

appContext.invite.detail.joined_other.description: The second line on a row of the list of invite links in the Invite pane of the app menu: how many people actually got in through this link. {{count}} is that number.

appContext.invite.detail.used.description: One of two facts on a row of the list of invite links in the Invite pane of the app menu, joined by a middle dot: how many of the link's uses are taken. {{used}} is how many people followed it (each use is spent whether they got in or are still waiting), {{max}} how many it allows.

appContext.invite.detail.anyone.description: One of two facts on a row of the list of invite links in the Invite pane of the app menu, joined by a middle dot: the link has no limit of people. Lower case; it follows the first fact. How many came in through it is the row's second line.

appContext.invite.detail.expired.description: One of two facts on a row of the list of invite links in the Invite pane of the app menu, joined by a middle dot: the link's end date has passed, so it no longer works. Lower case; it follows the first fact.

appContext.invite.detail.usedUp.description: One of two facts on a row of the list of invite links in the Invite pane of the app menu, joined by a middle dot: every use of the link is taken, so it no longer works. Lower case; it follows the first fact.

appContext.invite.detail.turnedOff.description: One of two facts on a row of the list of invite links in the Invite pane of the app menu, joined by a middle dot: someone turned the link off, or its maker can no longer grant what it grants, so it no longer works. Lower case; it follows the first fact.

appContext.invite.detail.noEnd.description: One of two facts on a row of the list of invite links in the Invite pane of the app menu, joined by a middle dot: the link never expires. Lower case; it follows the first fact.

appContext.invite.detail.underDay.description: One of two facts on a row of the list of invite links in the Invite pane of the app menu, joined by a middle dot: the link expires in less than a day. Lower case; it follows the first fact.

appContext.invite.detail.daysLeft_one.description: One of two facts on a row of the list of invite links in the Invite pane of the app menu, joined by a middle dot: how many days until the link expires. {{count}} is that number. Lower case; it follows the first fact.

appContext.invite.detail.daysLeft_other.description: One of two facts on a row of the list of invite links in the Invite pane of the app menu, joined by a middle dot: how many days until the link expires. {{count}} is that number. Lower case; it follows the first fact.

appContext.invite.detail.pair.description: The line on a row of the list of invite links in the Invite pane of the app menu: two facts about one link, side by side. {{uses}} is how many people have joined through the link, already worded, for example "3 of 25 joined", "4 joined" or "No one joined yet"; {{expiry}} is how long it still works, already worded, for example "7 days left" or "no end date". Keep the middle dot between them, or use the separator this language puts between two short facts.

appContext.invite.detail.waiting_one.description: The middle fact on a row of the list of invite links in the Invite pane of the app menu, between what the link has been used for and how long it works: how many people followed this link and have not got in yet, for example still on the waitlist or without a verified phone. {{count}} is that number. Shown only when it is not zero.

appContext.invite.detail.waiting_other.description: The middle fact on a row of the list of invite links in the Invite pane of the app menu, between what the link has been used for and how long it works: how many people followed this link and have not got in yet, for example still on the waitlist or without a verified phone. {{count}} is that number. Shown only when it is not zero.

appContext.invite.detail.triple.description: The line on a row of the list of invite links in the Invite pane of the app menu when people are still waiting on the link: three facts, side by side. {{uses}} is how much the link has been used, already worded; {{waiting}} is how many people have not got in yet, already worded, for example "1 waiting"; {{expiry}} is how long it still works, or why it no longer works, already worded. Keep the middle dots between them, or use the separator this language puts between short facts.

appContext.invite.detail.ended.expired.description: The last fact on a row of the list of invite links in the Invite pane of the app menu, in place of how long the link still works: the link's end date has passed. Lower case; it follows the first fact.

appContext.invite.detail.ended.usedUp.description: The last fact on a row of the list of invite links in the Invite pane of the app menu, in place of how long the link still works: every use it allowed is taken. Lower case; it follows the first fact.

appContext.invite.detail.ended.revoked.description: The last fact on a row of the list of invite links in the Invite pane of the app menu, in place of how long the link still works: somebody turned the link off. Lower case; it follows the first fact.

appContext.invite.title.description: Title of the Invite pane of the app menu. {{project}} is the project's (app's) name.

appContext.invite.titleUnnamed.description: Title of the Invite pane of the app menu. Used when the project's name has not loaded; "this app" is written as the pane has always shown it.

appContext.invite.making.description: Screen-reader text for the placeholder shown in the Invite pane of the app menu while the person's invite link is being created.

appContext.invite.copyFailed.text: Could not copy. Press and hold the link to copy it.
appContext.invite.copyFailed.description: Error in the Invite pane of the app menu when copying the invite link to the clipboard failed.

appContext.invite.shareTitle.description: Title handed to the device's share sheet when the person shares an invite link. {{project}} is the project's (app's) name. "Join" is a verb.

appContext.invite.shareTitleUnnamed.description: Title handed to the device's share sheet when the person shares an invite link. Used when the project's name has not loaded; "this app" is written as the pane has always shown it.

appContext.invite.noProject.text: Open a project to invite people to it.
appContext.invite.noProject.description: Shown in the Invite pane of the app menu when it is opened with no project in context. "Open" is a verb.

appContext.invite.buildersOnly.text: Only the people building {{project}} can invite others to it.
appContext.invite.buildersOnly.description: Shown in the Invite pane of the app menu to someone who may not make invite links, on a project where building is by invitation. {{project}} is the project's name.

appContext.invite.buildersOnlyUnnamed.text: Only the people building this app can invite others to it.
appContext.invite.buildersOnlyUnnamed.description: Shown in the Invite pane of the app menu to someone who may not make invite links, on a project where building is by invitation. Used when the project's name has not loaded; "this app" is written as the pane has always shown it.

appContext.invite.joinFirst.text: Join {{project}} to invite people to it.
appContext.invite.joinFirst.description: Shown in the Invite pane of the app menu to someone who is not a member yet and so may not make invite links. {{project}} is the project's name. "Join" is a verb.

appContext.invite.joinFirstUnnamed.text: Join this app to invite people to it.
appContext.invite.joinFirstUnnamed.description: Shown in the Invite pane of the app menu to someone who is not a member yet and so may not make invite links. Used when the project's name has not loaded; "this app" is written as the pane has always shown it.

appContext.invite.linkLabel.description: Accessible name of the read-only box in the Invite pane of the app menu that holds the invite link's address.

appContext.invite.copied.description: Text of the "Copy link" button in the Invite pane of the app menu for a moment after the link was copied.

appContext.invite.copyLink.description: Main button in the Invite pane of the app menu: a verb, copies the invite link to the clipboard.

appContext.invite.share.description: Second button in the Invite pane of the app menu: a verb, opens the device's share sheet with the invite link.

appContext.invite.expiresAfter.description: Label of the drop-down in the Invite pane of the app menu that sets how long a new invite link works. Its options follow it: 1 day, 7 days, Until you turn it off.

appContext.invite.option.untilOff.description: Option in the "Expires after" drop-down in the Invite pane of the app menu: the new link never expires.

appContext.invite.option.days_one.description: Option in the "Expires after" drop-down in the Invite pane of the app menu. {{count}} is the number of days the new link works.

appContext.invite.option.days_other.description: Option in the "Expires after" drop-down in the Invite pane of the app menu. {{count}} is the number of days the new link works.

appContext.invite.worksFor.description: Label of the drop-down in the Invite pane of the app menu that sets how many people a new invite link lets in. Its options follow it: 1 person, 25 people, Anyone with the link.

appContext.invite.option.anyone.description: Option in the "Works for" drop-down in the Invite pane of the app menu: the new link has no limit of people.

appContext.invite.option.people_one.description: Option in the "Works for" drop-down in the Invite pane of the app menu. {{count}} is how many people the new link lets in.

appContext.invite.option.people_other.description: Option in the "Works for" drop-down in the Invite pane of the app menu. {{count}} is how many people the new link lets in.

appContext.invite.makeNew.description: Button in the Invite pane of the app menu, under the two drop-downs: creates a new invite link with the chosen duration and limit, replacing the person's current one.

appContext.invite.change.description: Small link beside the heading of the invite links list in the Invite pane of the app menu: a verb, unfolds the two drop-downs that set how long a new link works and for how many people.

appContext.invite.liveLinks.description: Small heading in the Invite pane of the app menu over the list of every invite link, the ones that still work first and the ones that ended in the last 30 days after them, shown to someone who manages the project.

appContext.invite.yourLinks.description: Small heading in the Invite pane of the app menu over the list of the person's own invite links.

appContext.invite.madeBy.description: Small line on a row of the list of invite links in the Invite pane of the app menu: who made the link. {{username}} is that person's username; keep the @ before it.

appContext.invite.status.waiting_one.description: The second line on a row of the list of invite links in the Invite pane of the app menu, beside the joined count: how many people followed this link and are still waiting to get in. {{count}} is that number.

appContext.invite.status.waiting_other.description: The second line on a row of the list of invite links in the Invite pane of the app menu, beside the joined count: how many people followed this link and are still waiting to get in. {{count}} is that number.

appContext.invite.status.nobody.description: The second line on a row of the list of invite links in the Invite pane of the app menu when nobody has used the link at all: no one has joined and no one is waiting.

appContext.invite.status.pair.description: The second line on a row of the list of invite links in the Invite pane of the app menu, when people have both joined through the link and are waiting: the joined count, already worded, for example "2 joined", then the waiting count, for example "1 waiting". Keep the middle dot between them, or use the separator this language puts between two short facts.

appContext.invite.turnOff.description: Button on a row of the list of invite links in the Invite pane of the app menu: revokes that link so it stops working.

appContext.about.contributor.live_one.description: Shown at the right of a contributor's row in the About pane of the app menu: how many of that person's changes have been released. {{count}} is that number; "live" is an adjective.

appContext.about.contributor.live_other.description: Shown at the right of a contributor's row in the About pane of the app menu: how many of that person's changes have been released. {{count}} is that number; "live" is an adjective.

appContext.about.contributor.creator.description: Shown at the right of a contributor's row in the About pane of the app menu, for the person who made the app, when none of their changes have been released yet.

appContext.about.contributor.creatorLive.description: Shown at the right of a contributor's row in the About pane of the app menu, for the person who made the app: they made it, and {{count}} of their changes have been released. "live" is an adjective.
Shown at the right of a contributor's row in the About pane of the app menu, for the person who made the app: they made it, and {{count}} of their changes have been released. "live" is an adjective.

appContext.about.contributors.showFewer.description: Button under the contributors list in the About pane of the app menu, once the whole list is shown: folds it back to the first five.

appContext.about.contributors.showAll_on.description: Button under the contributors list in the About pane of the app menu: unfolds the whole list. {{count}} is how many contributors there are (more than five in practice).

appContext.about.contributors.showAll_ot.description: Button under the contributors list in the About pane of the app menu: unfolds the whole list. {{count}} is how many contributors there are (more than five in practice).

appContext.about.lineage.linkTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Remixed from" link in the About pane of the app menu. A remix is an app made as a copy of another; {{app}} is the original app's name. "open" is a verb.

appContext.about.lineage.linkTitleDelete.description: Tooltip of the "Remixed from" link in the About pane of the app menu. A remix is an app made as a copy of another; Used when the original app has been deleted; the app is shown as the word "deleted" in angle brackets, as it always has been. {{open}} and {{close}} are the angle brackets < and > that the code puts around the word; keep them around the translated word.

appContext.about.lineage.remixedFrom.description: Amber line under an app's description in the About pane of the app menu: this app was made as a copy (a remix) of another. {{app}} is the original app's name. Keep the fork sign first.

appContext.about.lineage.remixedFromDele.description: Amber line under an app's description in the About pane of the app menu: this app was made as a copy (a remix) of another. Used when the original app has been deleted; the app is shown as the word "deleted" in angle brackets, as it always has been. {{open}} and {{close}} are the angle brackets < and > that the code puts around the word; keep them around the translated word.

appContext.about.lineage.goneTitle.text: The original app no longer exists
appContext.about.lineage.goneTitle.description: Tooltip of the "Remixed from" line in the About pane of the app menu when the app it was copied from has been deleted.

appContext.about.added.description: Text of the disabled button in the About pane of the app menu, beside a check mark, once the app is in the person's My apps list.

appContext.about.addToMyApps.description: Button in the About pane of the app menu: adds this app to the person's own list of apps on Home. "My apps" is that list's name.

appContext.about.invite.description: Button in the About pane of the app menu, beside Added or Add to My apps, for a member of the app's community. A verb: opens the pane that makes an invite link to the community.

appContext.about.contributors.heading.description: Heading and accessible name of the section in the About pane of the app menu that lists the people whose changes went into the app.

appContext.about.contributors.loading.description: Shown under the Contributors heading in the About pane of the app menu while the list loads.

appContext.about.contributors.failed.description: Shown under the Contributors heading in the About pane of the app menu when the list could not be loaded.

appContext.about.contributors.none.description: Shown under the Contributors heading in the About pane of the app menu when nobody's change has gone into the app yet.

appContext.about.more.description: Heading and accessible name of the last section in the About pane of the app menu, which holds Share, Add to home screen, Code, Remix and the version.

appContext.about.addToHomeScreen.description: Row under More in the About pane of the app menu: puts an icon for this app (or for Homeroom) on the phone's home screen, or shows how.

appContext.about.code.description: Row under More in the About pane of the app menu: a noun, a link to the app's source code (on GitHub, or on Homeroom's own git host).

appContext.about.codePublic.description: Small note at the right of the Code row in the About pane of the app menu, for an app whose code is on GitHub: the source code is publicly readable there.

appContext.about.remix.description: Row under More in the About pane of the app menu: a verb, makes the person their own copy of this app to change.

appContext.about.remixSub.description: Second line of the Remix row in the About pane of the app menu.

appContext.about.liveSince.description: Tooltip of the version line in the About pane of the app menu. {{when}} is the date and time the running version was released, already formatted.

appContext.thisApp.description: Stands where the app's name is shown on its own at the top of the app menu when the name has not loaded. Shown alone, as a label; lower case in English. Sentences that name the app have unnamed wordings of their own.

appContext.title.description: Title at the top of the app menu (the sheet opened from the Homeroom mark in the header), above the app's name: what the menu is for, which is giving feedback on the app and finding out about it.

appContext.opensOutside.description: Read by screen readers only, after a link in the app menu that leaves Homeroom (the privacy notice, an app's code, or the browser), where a small box-with-arrow glyph is shown.

appContext.sheetLabel.description: Accessible name of the app menu: the sheet opened from the app's name in the header. A noun.

appContext.backToMenu.description: Accessible name of the back button at the top of the About and Invite panes of the app menu: returns to the menu's first page. {{app}} is the app's name.

appContext.backToThisAppMenu.description: Accessible name of the back button at the top of the About and Invite panes of the app menu, when the app's name is not known.

appContext.backToAbout.description: Accessible name of the back button at the top of the Invite pane of the app menu, when it was opened from the About pane: returns to that pane. {{app}} is the app's name; "About {{app}}" is that pane's name in the menu.

appContext.backToAboutThisApp.description: Accessible name of the back button at the top of the Invite pane of the app menu, when it was opened from the About pane and the app's name is not known.

appContext.goToHomeroom.title.description: Row in the app menu (the sheet opened from the app's name in the header) shown to someone who arrived through an app's invite link: leaves the app for Homeroom's own Home screen.

appContext.goToHomeroom.sub.text: Your Home, your communities and Homeroom bot
appContext.goToHomeroom.sub.description: Second line of the "Go to Homeroom" row in the app menu (the sheet opened from the app's name in the header): what is there. Home is the Home screen; Homeroom bot is Homeroom's assistant, a name.

appContext.addAppToHomeScreen.text: Add this app to your home screen
appContext.addAppToHomeScreen.description: Row in the app menu (the sheet opened from the app's name in the header) shown to a newcomer on a phone: opens the page that puts the app they are in (not Homeroom) on the phone's home screen as its own icon.

appContext.row.addHomeroom.text: Add Homeroom to your home screen
appContext.row.addHomeroom.description: Row in the app menu (the sheet opened from the Homeroom mark in the header) on a phone where Homeroom is not on the home screen yet: shows how to put Homeroom itself on the phone's home screen as an icon.

appContext.row.community.description: Row in the app menu (the sheet opened from the app's name in the header): opens the hub page of the community that owns this app.

appContext.row.toVote_one.description: Shown at the right of the "Go to community" row in the app menu (the sheet opened from the app's name in the header), also its tooltip and accessible name: how many proposals wait for this person's vote. {{count}} is that number.

appContext.row.toVote_other.description: Shown at the right of the "Go to community" row in the app menu (the sheet opened from the app's name in the header), also its tooltip and accessible name: how many proposals wait for this person's vote. {{count}} is that number.

appContext.row.terminal.description: Row in the app menu (the sheet opened from the app's name in the header), shown to developers: opens a command-line terminal for this app.

appContext.row.about.description: Row in the app menu (the sheet opened from the app's name in the header): opens the About pane, with the app's description, contributors and version. {{app}} is the app's name.

appContext.row.aboutThisApp.description: Row in the app menu (the sheet opened from the app's name in the header) when the app's name is not known: opens the About pane.

appContext.reportApp.description: Small link at the foot of the app menu, beside a flag: a verb, reports this app to Homeroom's moderators.

appContext.privacy.description: Small link at the foot of the app menu (the sheet opened from the app's name in the header), before "Report app": opens Homeroom's privacy notice in a new tab.

sidePanel.expandLabel.text: Open full width, leaving the app
sidePanel.expandLabel.description: Accessible name of the expand button in the header of the side panel (the pane docked beside an app on a wide screen, showing a conversation or a Workshop page): shows the panel's page on the whole screen instead of beside the app. "Open" is a verb.

sidePanel.expand.description: Tooltip of the expand button in the header of the side panel (the pane docked beside an app on a wide screen, showing a conversation or a Workshop page). "Open" is a verb.

sidePanel.close.description: Tooltip and accessible name of the ✕ button in the header of the side panel (the pane docked beside an app on a wide screen, showing a conversation or a Workshop page): a verb, closes the panel.

sidePanel.frameTitle.description: Accessible title of the embedded page inside the side panel, the pane docked beside an app on a wide screen.

sidePanel.resize.description: Accessible name of the draggable edge of the side panel (the pane docked beside an app on a wide screen, showing a conversation or a Workshop page).

sidePanel.resizeTitle.text: Drag to resize · double-click to reset
sidePanel.resizeTitle.description: Tooltip of the draggable edge of the side panel (the pane docked beside an app on a wide screen, showing a conversation or a Workshop page). Keep the middle dot between the two hints.

sidePanel.title.workshop.description: Title in the header of the side panel (the pane docked beside an app on a wide screen) when it shows a project's community page, its board of changes and requests. A noun.

sidePanel.title.proposal.description: Title in the header of the side panel (the pane docked beside an app on a wide screen) when it shows one proposal, a change put up for the community's vote. A noun.

sidePanel.title.request.description: Title in the header of the side panel (the pane docked beside an app on a wide screen) when it shows one request, a member's filed suggestion or bug report. A noun.

sidePanel.title.change.description: Title in the header of the side panel (the pane docked beside an app on a wide screen) when it shows one code change that is being worked on. A noun.

sidePanel.title.newChange.description: Title in the header of the side panel (the pane docked beside an app on a wide screen) when it shows the page where a new code change is started. "change" is a noun.

sidePanel.title.thread.description: Title in the header of the side panel (the pane docked beside an app on a wide screen) when it shows a conversation whose own name has not loaded. The name of the Messages screen.

sidePanel.title.agent.description: Title in the header of the side panel (the pane docked beside an app on a wide screen) when it shows a conversation with the coding agent whose own title has not loaded.

sidePanel.title.messages.description: Title in the header of the side panel (the pane docked beside an app on a wide screen) when it shows the inbox. The name of the Messages screen.

appFrame.cover.opening.description: Note under an app's icon and name on the cover shown while the app is being opened.

appFrame.cover.failed.title.description: Title of the failed card that replaces the waiting state on the cover shown while an app opens, when the app could not be opened. A "Try again" button follows.

appFrame.cover.failed.detail.text: It didn't finish loading. Check your connection and try again.
appFrame.cover.failed.detail.description: Second line of the failed card on the cover shown while an app opens. A "Try again" button follows it.

appFrame.waiting.title.description: Small heading over the "While you wait" card a member sees on the App tab while a project's first version is not ready yet. The card lists things to do in the meantime.

appFrame.waiting.sayHi.title.description: First row of the "While you wait" card a member sees on the App tab while a project's first version is not ready yet: opens the project's Discussion so the member can greet the others.

appFrame.waiting.sayHi.makerNote.description: Second line of the "Say hi to the group" row on the "While you wait" card a member sees on the App tab while a project's first version is not ready yet: the first thing the project's maker wrote in its Discussion. {{maker}} is their username and {{note}} what they wrote, in their own words. Use your language's quotation marks.

appFrame.waiting.sayHi.introduce.description: Second line of the "Say hi to the group" row on the "While you wait" card a member sees on the App tab while a project's first version is not ready yet, when the project's maker has not written anything yet.

appFrame.waiting.plan.title.description: Row of the "While you wait" card a member sees on the App tab while a project's first version is not ready yet: opens the plan for the first version, to read. "Plan" is a noun.

appFrame.waiting.plan.count_one.description: Second line of the "See the plan" row on the "While you wait" card a member sees on the App tab while a project's first version is not ready yet: how many lines the plan has. {{count}} is that number. "It" is the app being built.

appFrame.waiting.plan.count_other.description: Second line of the "See the plan" row on the "While you wait" card a member sees on the App tab while a project's first version is not ready yet: how many lines the plan has. {{count}} is that number. "It" is the app being built.

appFrame.waiting.plan.talk.description: Button at the foot of the plan sheet a member opens from the App tab while a project's first version is built: turns the sheet into the project's Discussion, to say something about the plan. "It" is the plan; "Discussion" is the name of the project's chat.

appFrame.waiting.suggest.title.description: Last row of the "While you wait" card a member sees on the App tab while a project's first version is not ready yet: opens the form for suggesting an improvement to the project.

appFrame.waiting.suggest.sub.text: Homeroom bot starts on it once it’s live
appFrame.waiting.suggest.sub.description: Second line of the "Suggest something" row on the "While you wait" card a member sees on the App tab while a project's first version is not ready yet. "Homeroom bot" is the name of Homeroom's assistant and stays as it is. The first "it" is the suggestion; the second is the project's first version, and "live" means built and running.

appFrame.waiting.sheet.discussion.description: Title of the sheet a member opens from the App tab, while a project's first version is not ready yet, to talk with the project's other members. {{project}} is the project's name. "Discussion" is a noun.

appFrame.waiting.sheet.plan.description: Title of the sheet a member opens from the App tab, while a project's first version is not ready yet, to read the plan for that version. {{project}} is the project's name.

appFrame.waiting.buildNote.description: Note after the status "Building it" on the App tab and in the plan sheet, for a member waiting for a project's first version: how long building one usually takes. Lower case, it follows the status on the same line; "min" abbreviates minutes.

appFrame.waiting.discussion.loading.description: Shown in the Discussion sheet a member opens from the App tab while the project's Discussion is being fetched.

appFrame.waiting.discussion.failed.text: The discussion could not be opened. Try again in a moment.
appFrame.waiting.discussion.failed.description: Shown in the Discussion sheet a member opens from the App tab when the project's Discussion could not be fetched.

appFrame.screens.pill.firstLook.text: First look · drawn from the plan
appFrame.screens.pill.firstLook.description: Small label over the picture area at the top of a project's card on the App tab while the project's first version is being built, when the picture is a first look at the app's main screen, drawn from the plan before anything is built.

appFrame.screens.pill.real.description: Small label over the picture area at the top of a project's card on the App tab while the project's first version is being built, when the picture is a screenshot of the app as built so far and the time it was taken is not known.

appFrame.screens.pill.realMinutes_one.description: Small label over the picture area at the top of a project's card on the App tab while the project's first version is being built, when the picture is a screenshot of the app as built so far. {{count}} is how many minutes ago it was taken; "min" abbreviates minutes.

appFrame.screens.pill.realMinutes_other.description: Small label over the picture area at the top of a project's card on the App tab while the project's first version is being built, when the picture is a screenshot of the app as built so far. {{count}} is how many minutes ago it was taken; "min" abbreviates minutes.

appFrame.screens.pill.realHours_one.description: Small label over the picture area at the top of a project's card on the App tab while the project's first version is being built, when the picture is a screenshot of the app as built so far. {{count}} is how many hours ago it was taken; "h" abbreviates hours.

appFrame.screens.pill.realHours_other.description: Small label over the picture area at the top of a project's card on the App tab while the project's first version is being built, when the picture is a screenshot of the app as built so far. {{count}} is how many hours ago it was taken; "h" abbreviates hours.

appFrame.screens.alt.firstLook.text: A first look at {{project}}, drawn from the plan
appFrame.screens.alt.firstLook.description: Text alternative of the picture in the picture area at the top of a project's card on the App tab while the project's first version is being built, when it is a first look at the app's main screen drawn from the plan. {{project}} is the project's name.

appFrame.screens.alt.real.description: Text alternative of one of the screenshots in the picture area at the top of a project's card on the App tab while the project's first version is being built, taken of the app as built so far. {{project}} is the project's name; {{number}} is this screenshot's place among them and {{total}} how many there are.

appFrame.screens.dot.description: Accessible name of one of the page dots under the screenshots in the picture area at the top of a project's card on the App tab while the project's first version is being built: shows that screenshot. {{number}} is its place and {{total}} how many there are. "Screen" is a noun: a screen of the app.

appFrame.live.switch.label.description: Accessible name of the two-way switch (Preview, Live) in the corner of the picture area at the top of a project's card on the App tab while the project's first version is being built.

appFrame.live.switch.preview.description: One side of the two-way switch in the corner of the picture area at the top of a project's card on the App tab while the project's first version is being built: the picture shows the first look drawn from the plan. A noun.

appFrame.live.switch.live.description: One side of the two-way switch in the corner of the picture area at the top of a project's card on the App tab while the project's first version is being built: the picture shows the app itself as it takes shape, updating as it is built. An adjective.

appFrame.live.sampleData.description: Small label in the bottom-left corner of the picture area at the top of a project's card on the App tab, while the picture shows the project's app running as it is built: the app is filled with made-up example content, not real people's information. A short noun phrase in a small rounded label.

appFrame.live.pill.starting.description: Small label over the picture area at the top of a project's card on the App tab while the project's first version is being built, with Live chosen, until the first picture of the running app arrives.

appFrame.live.pill.failed.text: A restart failed · showing the last good screen
appFrame.live.pill.failed.description: Small label over the picture area at the top of a project's card on the App tab while the project's first version is being built, with Live chosen, when the app being built did not start again after its latest change, so the picture is from before it.

appFrame.live.pill.ended.description: Small label over the picture area at the top of a project's card on the App tab, once the project's first version has been built, while it is reviewed, checked and tried: the picture is the app as it last looked while it was being built, kept there and no longer updating.

appFrame.live.pill.justUpdated.description: Small label over the picture area at the top of a project's card on the App tab while the project's first version is being built, with Live chosen, when the picture of the running app changed within the last few seconds. "Live" is an adjective.

appFrame.live.pill.updatedSeconds_one.description: Small label over the picture area at the top of a project's card on the App tab while the project's first version is being built, with Live chosen. "Live" is an adjective. {{count}} is how many seconds ago the picture of the running app last changed; "s" abbreviates seconds.

appFrame.live.pill.updatedSeconds_other.description: Small label over the picture area at the top of a project's card on the App tab while the project's first version is being built, with Live chosen. "Live" is an adjective. {{count}} is how many seconds ago the picture of the running app last changed; "s" abbreviates seconds.

appFrame.live.pill.updatedMinutes_one.description: Small label over the picture area at the top of a project's card on the App tab while the project's first version is being built, with Live chosen. "Live" is an adjective. {{count}} is how many minutes ago the picture of the running app last changed; "min" abbreviates minutes.

appFrame.live.pill.updatedMinutes_other.description: Small label over the picture area at the top of a project's card on the App tab while the project's first version is being built, with Live chosen. "Live" is an adjective. {{count}} is how many minutes ago the picture of the running app last changed; "min" abbreviates minutes.

appFrame.live.frame.starting.description: Text alternative of the phone-shaped picture in the picture area at the top of a project's card on the App tab while the project's first version is being built, with Live chosen, until the first picture of the running app arrives. {{project}} is the project's name.

appFrame.live.frame.live.description: Text alternative of the phone-shaped picture in the picture area at the top of a project's card on the App tab while the project's first version is being built, with Live chosen: it shows the app itself, updating as it is built. {{project}} is the project's name.

appFrame.live.frame.ended.text: {{project}}, as it last looked while it was built
appFrame.live.frame.ended.description: Text alternative of the phone-shaped picture in the picture area at the top of a project's card on the App tab, once the project's first version has been built, while it is reviewed, checked and tried: it shows the app as it last looked while it was being built. {{project}} is the project's name.

install.banner.getOnAppStore.text: Get the app on the App Store
install.banner.getOnAppStore.description: Second line of the install banner, the strip at the top of Homeroom in a phone's browser that offers the Homeroom app, when the link goes to Apple's App Store. "the App Store" is Apple's name for it.

install.banner.getOnGooglePlay.text: Get the app on Google Play
install.banner.getOnGooglePlay.description: Second line of the install banner, the strip at the top of Homeroom in a phone's browser that offers the Homeroom app, when the link goes to Google Play. Google Play is a name.

install.banner.getOnTestFlight.description: Second line of the install banner, the strip at the top of Homeroom in a phone's browser that offers the Homeroom app, when the link is an invitation to Apple's TestFlight beta programme. TestFlight is a name.

install.sentence.ios.text: Tap Share, then Add to Home Screen.
install.sentence.ios.description: One-line instruction in Homeroom's About pane on an iPhone or iPad: how to put Homeroom on the home screen. Share and Add to Home Screen are the names Safari shows; use the names the device shows in this language.

install.sentence.android.text: Open the browser menu, then Add to Home screen.
install.sentence.android.description: One-line instruction in Homeroom's About pane on an Android phone: how to put Homeroom on the home screen. Add to Home screen is the browser's own menu item; use the name the browser shows in this language.

install.ios.step1.description: Step 1 of 3 in the "Add Homeroom to your home screen" sheet on an iPhone or iPad; the Share icon is drawn beside it. Share is the name Safari gives the button.

install.ios.step2.description: Step 2 of 3 in the "Add Homeroom to your home screen" sheet on an iPhone or iPad. Add to Home Screen is the item in Safari's share menu; use the name the device shows in this language.

install.ios.step3.description: Step 3 of 3 in the "Add Homeroom to your home screen" sheet on an iPhone or iPad: after adding it, start Homeroom from the new icon. "Open" is a verb.

install.android.step1.text: Tap the menu in your browser's toolbar
install.android.step1.description: Step 1 of 3 in the "Add Homeroom to your home screen" sheet on an Android phone; the three-dot menu icon is drawn beside it.

install.android.step2.description: Step 2 of 3 in the "Add Homeroom to your home screen" sheet on an Android phone. Add to Home screen is the browser's own menu item; use the name the browser shows in this language.

install.android.step3.description: Step 3 of 3 in the "Add Homeroom to your home screen" sheet on an Android phone: after adding it, start Homeroom from the new icon. "Open" is a verb.

install.banner.getApp.description: Second line of the install banner, the strip at the top of Homeroom in a phone's browser that offers the Homeroom app, before it is known whether a store listing exists.

install.banner.addToHomeScreen.text: Add it to your home screen
install.banner.addToHomeScreen.description: Second line of the install banner, the strip at the top of Homeroom in a phone's browser that offers the Homeroom app, when there is no store listing: "it" is Homeroom, which can be added to the phone's home screen from the browser.

install.banner.how.description: Button on the install banner when Homeroom is added from the browser: opens the steps. Short for "How do I do that?".

install.banner.get.description: Button on the install banner: a verb, opens the app's store listing to download Homeroom.

install.banner.dismiss.description: Accessible name of the ✕ on the install banner, the strip at the top of Homeroom in a phone's browser: hides the strip.

install.steps.title.text: Add Homeroom to your home screen
install.steps.title.description: Title of the sheet that lists the three steps for putting Homeroom's icon on the phone's home screen.

install.steps.done.description: Button at the foot of the "Add Homeroom to your home screen" sheet: closes it once the steps are read.

session.attach.badgeFile.description: Small upper-case tag on an attached file's chip in an agent session when the file has no extension to show (other files show theirs, such as PDF or ZIP). Keep it short and in capitals.

appContext.invite.noLinks.description: Shown under the heading of the invite links list in the Invite pane of the app menu when no invite link was made or ended in the last 30 days, so the list has nothing to show.

session.changeRow.waitingForApproval.description: Where an agent session's current code change stands, on the session's row in Messages (after the change's name) and in the Homeroom menu's Agent chats: it is up for the community's vote.

session.changeRow.goingLive.description: Where an agent session's current code change stands, on the session's row in Messages (after the change's name) and in the Homeroom menu's Agent chats: it was approved and is being released.

session.changeRow.live.description: Where an agent session's current code change stands, on the session's row in Messages (after the change's name) and in the Homeroom menu's Agent chats: it has been released. An adjective.

session.changeRow.inProgress.description: Where an agent session's current code change stands, on the session's row in Messages (after the change's name) and in the Homeroom menu's Agent chats: it is being worked on and has not been put up for a vote.

session.release.line.description: Line in an agent session's changes panel, also the tooltip of the change's status pill, for a change merged into Homeroom itself that waits for the platform's next release. {{release}} is a sentence, without its full stop, saying when that release goes out, for example 'Merged; goes live in the next release (about 8 minutes)'. Keep the parameter and end the sentence as the language does.

topicBack.allItems.description: Text of the back chip at the top of a request's or proposal's page when it was opened from the project's All items page: it returns there. The name of that page.
